Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1578. GdS: Krösche announcement could come next week – how he will operate at Milan

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s plans.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

“Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

#1576. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1575. Monza vs Fiorentina - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 21 Nov 2026 09:32

Both battling at the wrong end of the Serie A standings, Monza and Fiorentina will vie for three precious points when matchday 12 comes to a close on Monday night.

While the hosts have slumped into the drop zone after four consecutive defeats, their Viola visitors are showing signs of revival.

Having lost six of their first eight games and recalled their former interim manager, Fiorentina had begun to steady the ship before international football intervened.

Paolo Vanoli's side have inched away from the relegation zone by claiming five points from their last three outings, with an away victory over Sassuolo being sandwiched by a pair of 2-2 home draws.

After sharing the spoils with Atalanta at the end of October, the Viola fought hard for a draw against old foes Juventus, taking the lead twice before settling for one point.

Both acceptable results in isolation, but Fiorentina's struggles at Stadio Franchi show no sign of ending: the Tuscan club's last league win on home turf dates back to April.

Now bound for Brianza, their two top-flight wins this term have both come on the road, so they will hope to pick up another on Monday.

However, sitting just two points above Monza, Fiorentina have yet to keep a clean sheet in Serie A and continue to look vulnerable at the back.

Across seven prior meetings in Monza, there have been three wins apiece, but the hosts have won two of the last three.

While precedent may suggest that they will come out on top, the Brianzoli departed for the international break on a dismal run of form.

Consecutive defeats to Torino, Napoli, Bologna and Atalanta left them stuck inside the drop zone, abruptly halting a relatively promising start.

Only Sassuolo have conceded more goals after 11 matchdays, leaving head coach Ivan Juric searching for solutions to his team's defensive woes.

Failing to score for the first time this season, the Serie B playoff winners were beaten 1-0 by La Dea last time out, continuing a grim top-flight record at Stadio Brianteo.

Dating back to their relegation campaign of 2024-25, Monza have won just three of their last 24 home games in Serie A.

Although expensive summer signing Arthur Atta is set to end a six-match absence, Fiorentina are still missing Fabiano Parisi and Marin Pongracic due to injury.

Alieu Njie returned from Sweden duty with a minor thigh problem, so Wilfried Gnonto or Pedro Goncalves could be promoted from the bench if required.

As part of an attacking trio, Njie has racked up five goal involvements from his last three Serie A appearances, while Argentine pair Mateo Pellegrino and Franco Mastantuono both have four goals this season.

Meanwhile, one man has been carrying Monza's attack: Capocannoniere leader and Liverpool target Gustavo Varela has scored more than half of their 17 league goals, netting nine in 10 games.

In the three-points-for-a-win era, only Fiorentina legend Gabriel Batistuta (13) and David Trezeguet of Juventus (10) have topped his tally for a newly promoted side after 11 matchdays.

Monza captain Matteo Pessina returned to full training during the break, having missed most of the campaign so far.

Former Fiorentina midfielder Michael Folorunsho has also recovered from a calf problem, but Yvan Maye and Jay Robinson are both doubts.

Tornqvist; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Lucchesi; Birindelli, Akinsanmiro, Foe Ondoa, Mangas; Mota, Robinson; Varela

De Gea; Jimenez, Dragusin, Viery, Mario; Ndour, Fagioli, Oulai; Mastantuono, Pellegrino, Gnonto

Fiorentina have equalled their worst defensive start to any Serie A season -  a negative record set back in 1933 - while Monza have never conceded more at this stage of a top-flight campaign.

They will surely share several goals on Monday night, but the Viola's vibrant attack should secure maximum points.

#1574. More games, less issues: How Milan’s current injury situation compares to one year ago

In the past few weeks, Ruben Amorim has been battling a long list of absences due to injuries, but how does it compare to one year ago?

The second international break brings a useful moment to pause and reflect on the injury issues within the squad. Given that there have been at times as many as eight players out, it feels as though Amorim has been rowing against the tide a bit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese asks for a physically demanding style and he consistently emphasises the importance of proper rotation. Yet, at present, the likes of Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Strahinja Pavlovic are all out.

From Stefano Pioli’s final years into Massimiliano Allegri’s one-season stint, there was a recurring problem of muscle issues. For example, last season – despite no European football – the Rossoneri suffered 31 total injuries during the season, leading to a crisis at certain points.

In the previous season, which included the Champions League, the figure hit 33. In Pioli’s last season in 2023-24, he battled a staggering 40 different issues. How does the current season compare to the last though? MilanNews provide the data.

1. Pulisic – Ankle sprain – July 26 to August 12, 17 days out during the summer. 2. Leao – Right calf elongational injury – August 17 to September 25, 39 days out and missed 5 games. 3. Jashari – Compound fracture of the right fibula – August 28 to October 30, 63 days out. 9 games missed so far. 4. Pavlovic – Flexor problem – from September 14 to September 18, 4 days out. 5. Maignan – Right calf problem – from September 14 to September 23, 9 days out and 1 game missed. 6. Tomori – Right aductor strain – from September 28 to October 3, 5 days out. 7. Saelemaekers – Right flexor injury – from October 11 to October 18, 7 days out. 8. Estupinan – Ankle problem – from October 11 to October 30, 19 days out and 3 games missed. 9. Pulisic – Right thigh hamstring injury – from October 11 to November 5, 25 days out and 4 games missed. 10. Rabiot – Left soleus injury – from October 16 to November 18, 33 days out and 5 games missed. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Muscle strain – October 18 to October 27, 9 days out and 2 games missed. 12. Nkunku – Toe problem – October 16 to October 23, 7 days out and 1 game missed. 13. Leao – Hip problem – October 28 to October 30, 2 days out. 14. Tomori – Knee problem – October 28 to November 1, 4 days out. 15. Gimenez – Ankle problem and arthroscopic surgery – October 28, 2025 to March 21, 2026, 114 days out and 22 games missed.

Total: Seven traumatic/other and eight muscular in 13 matches played (11 Serie A, 2 Coppa Italia).

1. Pulisic – Bone edema at the junction of the tibia and fibula, July 8 to August 21. 44 days out during preseason. 2. Gila – Right rectus femoris strain, July 25 to August 12. 18 days out during preseason. 3. Gabbia – Ankle problems, September 1 to 11. 10 days out and missed 1 game. 4. Saelemaekers – Right ankle problem and subsequent surgery, since September 29. 5. Gabbia – Left thigh flexor injury, with partial tendon involvement, since October 11. 6. Chukwueze – Left hip tensor fascia latae tendon rupture, resulting in surgery, since October 21. 7. Ramos – Calf muscle overload, October 21 to 23. 2 days out and missed 1 game. 8. Gila – Overuse inflammation in the left ankle, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 9. Rabiot – Right calf strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 10. Moreira – Left calf flexor strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Left medial flexor injury, from October 25. 12. Tomori – Right medial flexor injury, from October 29. 13. Pavlovic – Renal colic, from November 4 to 17. 13 days out and missed 2 games.

Total: Five traumatic/other and eight muscular from 15 matches played (11 Serie A, 4 Europa League).

So, while things might have felt quite bleak at various moments when gazing into a packed treatment room, Amorim has actually had a bit more luck than his predecessor when it comes to physical issues. Now he must hope that continues, or even that he gets luckier still.

#1573. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino target 'flattered' by fresh Old Trafford links

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 09:36

Galatasaray forward Victor Osimhen is allegedly 'flattered' by speculation linking him to Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Red Devils fixture on Sunday when his team face Liverpool at Anfield.

There is an argument that United need to enter the transfer market for a new left-back and centre-back over any other position.

However, with Benjamin Sesko sidelined in the long term, consideration will be given to adding a fresh face to the attack.

According to The Sun, Osimhen would be interested in taking an opportunity to move to Old Trafford.

The report claims that the Nigeria international is 'flattered' by suggestions that United could make a fresh move for his signature.

Osimhen has been linked with a transfer to the Premier League in the past, only for his wage demands or asking price at Napoli to allegedly provide a stumbling block.

Nevertheless, it is said that the 27-year-old still has ambitions to move to English football at some stage of his career.

As it stands, his contract at Galatasaray - which runs until the summer of 2029 - is likely to prevent any transfer from occurring in January.

That is seemingly partly a consequence of no release clause being present in his contract, while Galatasaray will not want to weaken their position in the Super Lig title race.

Ten goals and three assists have been contributed in his 11 appearances in Turkey's top flight and the Champions League this season.

Man United CEO Omar Berrada said in an interview with Sky Sports News this week that the club had been "disciplined" in the transfer market, and that is expected to remain the case.

Not only is Osimhen said to be on a contract at Galatasaray in the region of £13m per year, his club would demand in excess of £50m for his signature as a bare minimum.

United are unlikely to be able to afford those terms at this time, particularly when it is apparent that other positions need strengthening.

#1572. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Subs: Matthews, Tomiyasu, Mingueza, Doucoure, Lerma, Chilwell, Hughes, Gozo, McNeil

Subs: Walton, Kipre, Ouattara, Florentino, Nunez, Philogene, Maeda, Akpom, Flemming

Bournemouth XI: Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Scott, Adams; Tavernier, Kluivert, Rayan; Evanilson

Subs: Di Gregorio, Cook, Soler, Brooks, Christie, Gannon-Doak, Diakite, Toth, Rodriguez

Brentford XI: Kelleher; Hickey, Schuster, Ajer, Lewis-Potter; Yarmoliuk, Sangare, Janelt; Anthony, Schade, Thiago

#1570. Florian Wirtz scores twice (including a stunner) as Germany thump Netherlands 5-0 in UEFA Nations League... as Liverpool misfit receives a hug from Jurgen Klopp after impressing

Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.

The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.

And he continued that trend on Monday evening with two goals for his side to help them top their Nations League group.

His first was the pick of the bunch. Wirtz moved along the forward line as a Dutch side without Virgil van Dijk struggled to contain him. He picked up the ball around 25 yards out, cut inside onto his weaker left foot, and curled a pearling effort into the far corner off the post.

That goal, which came on the hour mark, put his side 2-0 up after Freiburg's Derry Scherhant had scored the opener, and Wirtz wasn't done there.

Centre back Nico Schlotterbeck made it 3-0 before the Liverpool man picked up his second of the night after drifting into the penalty box unmarked and finishing high after good work from Brajan Gruda.

Cette version de Wirtz avec le maillot de la Mannschaft c’est celle qu’on aimerait voir chaque semaine en PL. Quel missile pour faire le break ! Meilleur buteur allemand sur cette édition de l’UNL. 🇩🇪🔥 pic.twitter.com/m0DqaOungS

Florian Wirtz scored a brace for Germany as they thumped the Netherlands 5-0 in Nations League action

Liverpool midfielder Wirtz received a big hug from a smiling Jurgen Klopp at full time

Gruda himself, who is on loan at RB Leipzig from Brighton, wrapped up the five-star win on a night that arguably saw Klopp announce himself as Germany boss.

After full-time, the ex-Liverpool manager gave Wirtz a huge hug as the duo beamed with big smiles on their faces.

While it was a night to remember for Germany, a Netherlands team that included the likes of Micky van de Ven, Jurrien Timber and Wirtz's Liverpool team-mate Cody Gakpo were left exasperated.

Van Dijk had pulled out of the squad with a knock after playing with a knock in recent weeks.

His side will still, though, compete in the Nations League quarter-finals after finishing second in the group, finishing ahead of Greece on goal difference.

As for Wirtz, he will hope his performance will help continue what has been an uphill climb so far this season.

He also found the net for Germany in their first match of the international break – a 3-1 win over Serbia – and picked up a goal and assist in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

In total, he has two goals and five assists in 15 games for Liverpool this season – though the Reds will hope those numbers increase as the season goes on.

His second goal came as he drifted into the penalty area and finished high into the net

Last month, meanwhile, Reds manager Andoni Iraola insisted he has full faith in his midfielder.

'I think he has had a little bit of everything this season,' he said. 'He has had good games, probably the other day was not his best game, especially offensively. We trust Florian.

'Florian is a very good player. He was coming from good performances in the international break, I think. I think it is a matter of everyone to find his moment.'

Klopp hailed him 'exceptional', meanwhile, during the last international break.

#1569. Harry Kane injury could force Bayern Munich into £44m transfer dilemma amid Arsenal, Man United interest

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39

Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.

The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old was withdrawn after just 20 minutes, leaving Vincent Kompany without his first-choice centre-forward at a crucial stage of the campaign. The setback is particularly concerning given Bayern's limited options in the position and their demanding domestic and European schedule.

One player who could now become increasingly relevant to the German club's recruitment discussions is Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who has been monitored by Bayern scouts in recent weeks.

However, the 22-year-old's reported valuation of up to €50m (£44m), combined with Brugge's reluctance to sanction a winter departure, presents a significant obstacle should Bayern decide to bring forward their search for attacking reinforcements.

According to German newspaper TZ, Bayern have sent scouts to Belgium on several occasions to monitor Tresoldi, whose performances have attracted considerable attention across Europe.

The Germany Under-21 international has scored 14 goals and provided one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as one of the most productive young forwards on the continent.

His form has inevitably generated transfer speculation, with reports suggesting that Bayern view him as a potential long-term addition to their attacking department.

Significantly, the club's interest emerged before Kane suffered his injury against Koln.

Earlier this month, Bayern were reportedly exploring the possibility of signing Tresoldi as an additional attacking option despite having recently extended Kane's contract until 2029. The idea was to strengthen their squad with a younger centre-forward capable of developing alongside the England international.

That strategy could now face an unexpected test.

With Kane unavailable for several months, Bayern must decide whether their existing attacking resources can compensate for his absence or whether an immediate signing would provide greater security.

Tresoldi possesses several attributes that could appeal to Kompany, including his movement inside the penalty area, ability to attack space behind defenders and increasingly reliable finishing.

However, securing his signature midway through the campaign would be far from straightforward.

Reports in Belgium have indicated that Club Brugge are determined to retain the striker until at least the summer, with the club's hierarchy reluctant to entertain offers during the January transfer window.

According to Het Nieuwsblad, Brugge have made their position clear to interested clubs, although an exceptional financial proposal could potentially force a reassessment.

German reports have placed Tresoldi's potential price between €40m (£35m) and €50m (£44m), with the forward under contract until June 2029.

Bayern have not submitted a confirmed offer, and there is currently no evidence that Kane's injury has prompted formal negotiations with the Belgian club.

Any attempt to accelerate a move for Tresoldi could also bring Bayern into competition with several Premier League clubs.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with the Club Brugge striker, whose impressive scoring record has strengthened his reputation as one of Europe's most promising young centre-forwards.

That timeline broadly aligned with Bayern's previous interest, which appeared to concern the longer-term development of their attacking squad rather than an urgent winter acquisition.

Kane's injury introduces a potentially important difference in Bayern's circumstances, although it does not establish that the Bundesliga champions have changed their transfer strategy.

The club must also assess whether investing heavily in another centre-forward would make sense once Kane returns to fitness, particularly after committing to a new long-term agreement with their leading goalscorer.

Kompany has alternatives within his squad, but none offers the same combination of finishing, creativity and experience as the England captain.

A temporary tactical adjustment may therefore be necessary, with greater responsibility potentially falling on Bayern's other attacking players.

The German champions could also turn to their academy, where 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention following impressive performances for the youth teams.

According to Kicker, the teenager was already under consideration for greater involvement with the senior squad before Kane's injury, although expecting him to replace the England international immediately would represent a considerable leap.

For Bayern, the dilemma is therefore as much about timing as identifying the right player.

Tresoldi was already an attractive prospect before Kane's setback, but Brugge's reported resistance to a January sale means that accelerating the deal could prove expensive and difficult.

Meanwhile, Arsenal and Manchester United remain interested parties whose own plans have been linked to the summer window.

Bayern's next decision will depend on whether Kompany believes his squad can absorb Kane's absence or whether the club considers an early investment necessary to protect its ambitions in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

#1566. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

#1565. McKennie ruled out of AZ trip with adductor fatigue as Alajbegović and Cabal return

Weston McKennie will miss Thursday's Europa League game at AZ Alkmaar with fatigue in his right adductor, though he has no muscle tear. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal are fit again, a relief for a badly stretched squad before a demanding trip.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

McKennie lasted only the first half at the Allianz Stadium. Federico Gatti replaced him at the break. Luciano Spalletti had to send on an extra defender because McKennie felt a pull in his adductor. The coach also had few other players to choose from.

A short rest should be enough, because the injury is fatigue rather than a tear, Sky Sport Italia reported. He should be back for the league. The problem is in his right adductor. The medical staff will check him again before Thursday, ANSA said.

Alajbegović had both a goal and a scare against Napoli. He opened the scoring in the 70th minute and was replaced by Jérémie Boga two minutes later. Boga then added the second in the 87th. At 19 years and 41 days, the teenager has set a new mark: no non-Italian scorer in a Serie A meeting of these two clubs has been younger.

His knee knock has already cleared up. Cabal made way for Andrea Cambiaso after 83 minutes with cramp. That is put down to him not having started a game for some time. He will be available in Alkmaar.

The match at AZ kicks off at 21:00 CET on 5 November. It is Matchday 4 of the league phase. Juventus have two wins and a draw so far.

AZ will be hard to break down at home. Their last home defeat in Europe was 4-1 to Aston Villa in the Conference League in October 2023.

Juventus arrive in good scoring form. They have nine goals in this season’s Europa League. Only Benfica, with ten, have scored more. That is Juventus’s best total after three games of a European campaign since 1999/2000.

#1564. GdS: Cisse becomes a pillar as Amorim as experiments with four-man attack

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Milan had a very clear plan when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

The most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

In that sense, Cisse will be important as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

The average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes.  Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

At just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

#1563. Pep Guardiola visits Bahia in new City Football Group role

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

Guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

The visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

"I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them."

Almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

During their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us."

Guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, New York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

His journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

The visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been announced, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

Nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would currently secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

For Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.
