Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

#1535. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

#1534. Wayne Rooney reveals how two-day binge drinking sessions while at Man United left him considering suicide as he hit 'rock bottom' and risked pushing away wife Coleen

Published: 05:48 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:41 EST, 17 November 2026

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but says he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he said on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment

He said without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old

The Man United legend said he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career

'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney said. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

He previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'

He added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle

He also said part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

In his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney said: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

#1528. Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

#1526. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

RMC was not much kinder to Barcola as well, concluding: 'The Liverpool winger was one of the few to start both matches in November. But in the end, it didn't really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

'Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves. Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.'

Even newcomer Adrien Truffert was not afforded some sympathy as Jaquin said: 'After a rather satisfying debut in October, the Bournemouth left-back benefited from the trust of Zinedine Zidane, who played him in Italy. But despite his efforts, the Cherries player delivered a very mixed performance.'

This recent criticism adds to growing dissatisfaction in France with the overall state of the national team under Zidane.

Liverpool's £123million man is yet to make a major impact for club or country so far this season

Journalist Walid Acherchour made his feelings known on the After Foot programme, saying: 'Zidane hit a wall of reality with this second international break... I found the attitude of some individuals against Turkey to be very poor.

'In the second half against Italy and in the match against Turkey, how do you manage without the ball when you're being torn apart in midfield? Zidane will have to work on all these questions.'

Acherchour closed by saying bluntly: 'The honeymoon is over.'

After an ultimately disappointing World Cup in which the French were again by Spain in a major semi-final – following their Euro 2024 exit – long-term manager Didier Deschamps left after 14 years in charge.

Legendary midfielder Zidane succeeded him in the summer and has already led France to the top of their Nations League group – but some of his players may have to go much further to win over their critics.

#1522. Çelik pulled from Türkiye XI with left hamstring tightness as Kalulu is already out

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

An Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

If Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

The league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, in the following season, he bagged a whopping 29 league goals with the help of Luciano Spalletti’s trust and the assists from Francesco Totti and Mohamed Salah. His resurgence was remarkable, so it’s something Ramos can take inspiration from.

#1520. McKennie says USA players could follow Pochettino to Manchester United

Weston McKennie has said USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

The question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

McKennie called the speculation inevitable. He said many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

Pochettino was asked about the same subject. He said now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

Pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

The comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s plans and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

McKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

The club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

The next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

#1516. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Ipswich's first act of this game was to launch a long ball towards Marli Salmon and Zian Flemming. Salmon won the header, and then continued to win the overall battle with Flemming. Such an impressive performance by the 17yo. You don't see many defenders doing that at this age.

Arteta’s side are through to the fourth round of the League Cup.

Ipswich Town 2 Arsenal 4 (Akpom) Davis picks out Akpom who swivels to deceive Konsa before sweeping home. There was perhaps a foul in the build-up as Lewis-Skelly appeared to get held back by the goalscorer as he scrambled to get back.

Arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.

And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.

For those who are into your statistics, another Dowman goal here would create some history...

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4 (Mehmeti) Clarke makes an immediate impact, bursting down the left before cutting the ball back to Mehmeti who had just held his run and is able to beat Kepa from 10 yards out.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 4 (Merino) Arsenal work the ball infield from the right in instalments, Madueke feeding Zubimendi who passes through Dowman to Merino on the edge of the box who opens up his body before guiding the ball around Walton.

Arsenal are FLYING!Merino puts another goal away for the Gunners 🔥 pic.twitter.com/nrzHHk1bou

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Kepa stretches to claim a looped Flemming cross which had echoes of the Spaniard’s game-defining error in last year’s League Cup final. This time he collects with a minimum of fuss. That Flemming was so far out on the left will be of concern to O’Neil.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3 (Dowman) Madueke picks out Zubimendi in the box who in turn finds Dowman in the right half space and he gallops on to the ball before arrowing the ball past Walton. The assist had grazed Greaves’ outstretched arm and would surely have led to a penalty had Dowman not done the honours.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

Arsenal’s kick-off routines caused a stir last season, but this term they have mixed things up once more. Here, Zubimendi lays off Lewis-Skelly, who punches in a line-breaking pass to get Arsenal on the front foot from the off.

Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.

L: Peterborough United 2 Barnsley 2L: West Ham United 2 Fulham 2HT: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2HT: Liverpool 1 Tottenham Hotspur 0HT: Reading 0 Brentford 2

Liverpool are ahead against Spurs at Anfield thanks to this strike from Mac Allister:

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Arteta’s nine changes are looking fairly sensible now. He will be particularly pleased to have seen fringe players like Dowman and Madueke get on the scoresheet so emphatically. Arsenal will need their full squad to achieve their lofty goals this season and that half will give Arteta confidence that they have enough firepower to last the course.

We’ll play one minute of time added on...

Arsenal inject a bit of calm to proceedings with a healthy spell of possession. Their horizontal and vertical rotations (Lewis-Skelly is now minding to drop into that Rice role alongside the centre-backs) are proving tricky for Ipswich to track.

Gyokeres gets a shot away after a clever run in behind by Merino but cannot get enough pace behind his strike to trouble Walton.

Mehmeti brings down a searching ball from deep and faces up to Gabriel as he enters Arsenal box. Such is the Brazilian’s poise, though, that even when the Ipswich forward appears to have worked a yard of space, he telescopes in his leg and stops Mehmeti’s advances with perfunctory ease.

Ipswich are getting more bodies forward, with both full-backs bombing on. The ball is worked out to Furlong out on the right but, in a promising position, he loses his footing and the ball rolls out of play.

Next comes a foray down the left, Philogene beats Salmon on the outside but Kepa gets down smartly to cut out his cross. The next goal will naturally go a long way to determining how this tie plays out.

Ipswich are in the ascendancy and Greaves heads goalwards off a corner but does not get the requisite contact to beat Kepa. Arsenal launch a swift counter which is snuffed out by McAteer, illegally, and he goes into the book.

Ipswich might have thrown the towel in at 2-0 but they are pushing quite hard here and have caused Arsenal a few problems since the second goal. Philogene looks particularly dangerous on the left flank.

Outtara has been Ipswich’s best attacking outlet and he threads another lovely ball into the path of Philogene who is just beaten to it by Gabriel. The subsequent corner is punched away by Kepa.

Kepa goes long and Greaves misjudges the flight of the ball. Madueke looks to be in, but Ipswich’s centre-half recovers well and is able to block the eventual effort.

Merino picks out Dowman between the lines and the teenager is straight into Ipswich’s backline. His effort is well-struck but is charged down and cleared to safety.

Better from Ipswich! Their best shot at getting back into this contest is through counters when Arsenal are not set, and here Outtara bursts down the left before swinging in a deep cross to Flemming who cuts the ball back to Mehmeti who fires the ball just over the crossbar.

Guimaraes is slotting in between Arsenal’s split centre-backs in Arsenal’s build-up and Ipswich are not prepared to go three vs three that high up the pitch meaning the Brazilian has all the time in the world to dictate play from there. We’ve seen this all season long from Rice.

Arsenal are in complete control. Madueke flashes a delivery across the face of goal which is just cut out by Kipre before Gyokeres can get a foot in.

Arsenal’s midfield is so powerful and they showed it there, as Guimaraes slammed into one tackle and then Merino followed up with another to create the chance for Madueke. Arsenal are completely dominant here.

A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2 (Madueke) That is goal of Ipswich’s own making. Walton’s loose pass out is picked off by livewire Guimaraes, and Merino spins in a ball in behind for Madueke to stride on to and spear beyond Walton into the bottom corner.

Arsenal are flying 🔥Noni Madueke adds a second for the Gunners 🔴 pic.twitter.com/gAVmAI3odx

Florentino’s loose pass is picked off by Dowman and the youngster earns a free-kick as the Ipswich midfielder attempts to recover. It’s taken quickly and Eze bursts into the box - there is a half-hearted shout for a penalty as the ball appears to strike Ouattara’s arm but the contact appears incidental and the referee waves play on.

Max Dowman’s second goal for Arsenal is quite similar to his first, scored so thrillingly against Everton last season. On both occasions he has put an opposition defender face-first in the turf before scoring the goal. Outrageous ability with the ball at his feet.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

Ipswich earn a free-kick on the left by-line but Gyokeres does his job at the near post and heads away Nunez’s delivery.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1 (Dowman) Simply majestic. A simple one-two with Eze on the left has Dowman running at Ipswich’s defence. He drops his shoulder and sells Kipre a dream before stroking the ball beyond Walton. “1-0 to the champions” sing the travelling fans.

Lewis-Skelly bursts down the left and picks out Dowman on the edge of the box. He attempts to tee up Guimaraes but Nunez gets a toe in and is able to avert the danger.

Early indications suggest Zubimendi will play in the nominal right-back position, inverting into midfield when Arsenal build up.

Madueke picks up the ball on the right flank and drifts inside before Guimaraes’ effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Flemming gets us started. Ipswich kicking from right to left.

The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts. Last week Arsenal were made to change into red shorts to avoid a similar clash with Napoli, but apparently that’s no problem tonight. Modern football for ya!

Here’s a reminder of the line-ups in full:

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Here are tonight’s League Cup third-round matches:

L: Peterborough 1 Barnsley 1L: West Ham United 0 Fulham 08pm: Ipswich Town vs Arsenal8pm: Liverpool vs Tottenham Hotspur8pm: Reading vs Brentford

Aug 16: Arsenal 3 Manchester City 0 (Community Shield)Aug 21: Arsenal 3 Coventry City 0Aug 31: Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1Sep 6: Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1Sep 9: Napoli 0 Arsenal 1 (Champions League)Sep 12: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 2

Aug 22: Ipswich Town 2 Sunderland 1Aug 25: Ipswich Town 3 Leicester City 1Aug 30: Manchester United 5 Ipswich Town 2Sep 4: Ipswich Town 0 Liverpool 2Sep 12: Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3

Arsenal are warming up with Eze on the left, Madueke on the right and Dowman as the No 10 behind Gyokeres. In defence it looks like Zubimendi at right-back. The formation in the warm-up is not always the formation in the match, though...! They have played that trick before.

"You have to be patient with him" 🗣️Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady on Max Dowman's potential for Arsenal 🙌 pic.twitter.com/O2bU0SQoJn

"They merit a start from the way they train"Mikel Arteta on Marli Salmon and Max Dowman being given their first starts of the season in tonight's game at Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/yYbFXn2Oje

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1515. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

#1514. Amorim discusses ‘fun’ Frosinone, final third struggles and confirms Pavlovic’s return

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim’s plan appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause issues on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a big responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really important because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

“They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I said against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause issues.”

Camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

“Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

“Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini said himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games…

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed…

“That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really important for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

“Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your plan. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

“I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”

#1513. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

#1512. French team: the latest story from Kylian Mbappé

Kylian Mbappé decided to respond to criticism in his own way. While his withdrawal from the French team due to injury is being talked about, the Real Madrid striker published a story on Instagram in which we see him boarding a plane, dressed in the official Blues tracksuit, with Italy as an itinerary.

A publication which comes after his replacement in the French team group by Senny Mayulu. Zinédine Zidane had also confirmed his withdrawal on Wednesday at a press conference, on the eve of the Blues’ trip to Italy to face the Nazionale this Thursday evening in the League of Nations. Without speaking directly about the criticism of which he is the subject, the French captain thus displays his trip with the colors of the selection, despite his unavailability for this meeting.

#1510. Bayern Munich lose Kane and Olise before facing Lille

Big blow in prospect for Bayern Munich? During the draw conceded at home against Cologne (1-1), this Friday evening in the Bundesliga, the Bavarian club saw two of its major players leave prematurely the match against Cologne, this Friday evening. Harry Kane and Michael Olise were both hit.

The first had to give up his place in the 20th minute. After a duel with Joël Schmied in the area, the English striker remained on the ground, visibly injured in the left ankle. He attempted to continue the meeting for a few minutes, before finally requesting the change. Tom Bischof replaced him.

The scenario repeated itself with Michael Olise. The Frenchman was hit following contact with Tom Krauss in the 41st minute. Despite the treatment received on the pitch, the French winger limped to the locker room and did not return to the field after the break. Young Tim Binder took his place.

These two injuries come at the worst time for Vincent Kompany. The Bavarian coach already has to deal with several important absences, notably those of Serge Gnabry, Luis Diaz, Manuel Neuer, Alphonso Davies and Ismaël Saibari.

Very bad news for the German champions before the trip to Lille, scheduled for Wednesday in the Champions League. It remains to be seen the exact nature of Kane and Olise’s injuries, as well as their possible unavailability for this European meeting.

Francesco Camarda could join Cagliari on loan in January and as part of the deal, AC Milan could obtain an option for Paul Mendy, according to a report.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A loan seems to be the most likely option, especially if Milan were to bring in another striker, but the big question is where he should go. After a so-so loan spell at Lecce, the Rossoneri must evaluate carefully before making their choice.

#1508. Gary Neville launches surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

'(De Ligt has) got one big problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come quickly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's plan for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

#1506. Kean’s new tibia injury rules former Juventus striker out of Como v Juventus

Moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin. The former Juventus striker is set to miss about two more months, so he will not face his old club on 29 November.

Moise Kean has suffered a new tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The new problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s update described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

That plan has now collapsed. Kean had been out since early October. The original injury came while he was playing for Italy against France on 2 October. That match was the first leg of a Nations League tie.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

Without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

For Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.

Como 1907 is pleased to announce the signing of Italian international forward Moise Kean from @acffiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent.

Official statement ➡️ https://t.co/PJKnFXS9Xp pic.twitter.com/4F30ROYFUT

— Como1907 (@Como_1907) September 1, 2026

Luciano Spalletti’s side need results. Juventus sit six points behind fourth place and have averaged just over 1.6 points per game, according to Corriere dello Sport. The paper sees the run of fixtures as decisive for the push for a Champions League place. It warns that dropping points against Venezia would force Juventus to win every remaining game of 2026 to stay in touch with the top four.

The schedule offers little respite after the trip to Como. Juventus host Udinese on 6 December and Monza on 14 December. They then travel to Roma on 19 December.
